findings.what: The reused event kind no longer has one meaning: it previously denoted a D3 fail-closed page routed to an image asset, but now also denotes a detection-only page whose native output may ship. D3 pages also receive two same-kind events, inflating audit counts.
findings.why: The established producer at src/socr/pipeline/orchestrator.py:5469 and contract comment at src/socr/core/audit_log.py:104-107 define table_region_unverifiable as routed/fail-closed. Consumers and humans cannot distinguish output disposition from kind/count alone after this change. Use a distinct detection event or migrate the kind contract and de-duplicate the D3 emission explicitly.

findings.what: The claimed scope guard exercises only _phase_analyze and cannot fail if later process/assemble logic keys the new event on document status, metadata, escalation, or routing.
findings.why: Its assertions at lines 109-121 inspect immediate PageState fields only. The event is consumed later by build_tables_trust and document metadata assembly; a future or accidental downstream status/routing branch would pass this guard. The binding no-routing constraint needs an end-to-end process test, with the provider ladder patched for CI hermeticity.

findings.what: Empirical sample counts and a disputed sample-specific rate are hardcoded into source comments, tests, and runtime event detail.
findings.why: Project instructions prohibit hardcoding empirical data in source. Issue #205 also records that neither 25.3% nor 13.8% is 'the' rate. Runtime detail at lines 873-875 bakes the 62-page sample into every future document; describe the pending hand-judgement without sample-specific constants.

what_i_tried_to_break: Started with the modified GH-211 exhaustive assertion and confirmed it remains exhaustive and additively records a real second event, so that edit is legitimate. Traced every changed production line and found no direct page/document status, escalation, or routing mutation. Traced the reused kind through audit_log.py, tables_trust.py, metadata, CLI, and the pre-existing D3 producer; this exposed the semantic collision and duplicate same-kind D3 count. Inspected the scope guard and found it stops at _phase_analyze rather than exercising downstream consumers. Copied the new test to the pinned baseline, ran it with full isolation canary and PYTHONPATH, observed a behavioural F.. failure at the event assertion (not ImportError), deleted it, and verified the baseline worktree clean. No MagicMock-negative assertion is vacuous: assertions inspect concrete state/events returned after the stubbed detector call. The test does not drive _phase_agentic/process, so no provider patch is required for its current shape.
